records.method: Example B (tvui 0.2.1/0.2.2) perf log, 300-frame windows over ~90 s of use and 45 s idle
records.evidence: frame interval avg 16.66-16.84 ms with 186-209 views, 3-50 draw calls, 200-840 quads, 12-14 image textures; swap avg 1.1-1.4 ms (the vsync wait happens in the first GL call of the next frame, not in SDL_GL_SwapWindow)
records.limitations: 4-14 intervals per 300 exceed 20 ms even when idle; the average implies only ~1-2 truly dropped frames per 300, the rest is jitter made up by the next frame. Occasional 25-52 ms stalls inside SDL_PollEvent, cause unknown. Replacing a full-screen quad with a clear made no measurable difference.

records.method: Example B 0.4.0/0.4.1 with launch params {"wnkCrashTest":"segv"}, then a normal launch
records.evidence: record written to /tmp/<id>/crash.log (signal 11, code 2, fault address, state Running, version, build id, pc/lr/sp); the 32-bit ARM backtrace unwinds through the signal frame (handler, crash_now, run, main); tools/symbolize-crash.py resolves it to source lines; the next launch logs it
records.limitations: the firmware preloads /lib/libSegFault.so into the app; the kit's handler replaces its handlers

records.method: Example B perf log, two builds (0.2.2 and 0.4.0) A/B on the idle home screen
records.evidence: frame interval median 19.96-19.99 ms (50 Hz) in this session, versus 16.67 ms (60 Hz) in earlier sessions the same day; SDL_webOSGetRefreshRate kept reporting 120 (the panel's maximum, not the current output rate)

records.method: Example D (org.wnk.examples.player 0.1.x), libNDL_directmedia.so.1 dlopened
records.evidence: NDL_DirectMediaInit -> 0 (305-465 ms cold, 27-48 ms on later inits in the same process), NDL_DirectMediaLoad -> 0 (1.9 s on the first load after install, 80-170 ms afterwards), NDL_DirectVideoSetArea(0,0,1920,1080) -> 0; load callback 0x16 then 0x1a right after the first packets; 0x17 on unload
records.limitations: NDL_DirectMediaSetAppState(FOREGROUND) right after init returns -1; no 0x1c end-of-stream event with buffer feeding

records.method: Example D 0.1.0, packets fed as fast as accepted
records.evidence: a 15 s H.264+AAC clip (375 video, 704 audio packets) was accepted in 0.6 s with no non-zero return; fed that way the picture froze after a few seconds and no sound played
records.limitations: the app must pace feeding itself (the controller now keeps within 1 s of its playback clock)

records.method: Example D 0.1.1+, 1080p25 H.264 MP4 with AAC decoded to S16 stereo PCM 48 kHz, paced feeding

records.method: Example D 0.1.1, MPEG-TS H.264 + MP3 (mono 48 kHz) loaded as NDL_AUDIO_TYPE_MP3

records.method: Example D 0.1.2, the same H.264+AAC clip fed with microsecond and with millisecond PTS, paced in real time

records.method: Example D, NDL PCM info format "S16LE", layout "interleaved", channelMode "stereo", 48 kHz enum

records.method: Example A 0.7.0 (requiredPermissions database.operation, securitykey.operation), SecretStore probe via luna://com.webos.service.keymanager3/generateKey
records.evidence: errorCode -1 "Service does not exist: com.webos.service.keymanager3."; the plain envelope in DB8 round-trips and survived a relaunch

records.method: Example A 0.7.1 WebSocket probe (CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY + curl_easy_send/recv, libcurl/7.61.0) against tests/integration/http_server.py --serve on the LAN
records.evidence: open in 68 ms; UTF-8 text echoed, a 3-fragment message reassembled, a 200000-byte binary message received, a server ping answered; 5 s of keepalive pings; client close 1000 echoed, clean

records.method: Example A 0.7.1 probe against wss://ws.postman-echo.com/raw (public echo server)
records.evidence: TLS (OpenSSL 1.1.1t, system CA store) and handshake in 1.5 s over the internet; UTF-8 text echoed
records.limitations: close not exercised against that server (the probe closes after a binary reply, which it does not send)

records.method: Example D 0.2.0, {"uri": "http://<LAN server>/files/..."}: 180 s 1080p25 H.264 + AAC MP4 (181 MB, index at the end) from tests/integration/http_server.py --serve
records.evidence: opened in 78 ms (range request to the index at the end, then back); picture and sound in sync (owner); 21 seeks of 10 s back to playing in 170-440 ms, backward ones with one range request each; frame interval 20.1 ms avg, no feed retries
records.limitations: LAN only, plain HTTP; HTTPS media, slow links and reconnects after drops not exercised on the TV

records.method: Example D 0.2.0, same server: 180 s 1080p25 H.264 + AAC MPEG-TS (186 MB)
records.evidence: plays from 0.02 s; every seek starts at a video keyframe (16.02, 27.02, 37.02, 47.02, 57.02 s) after 310-380 ms, 2-3 range requests each while stepping back
records.limitations: the picture goes black during each seek and pause: NDL v2 is unloaded and reloaded (no safe flush or pause)

records.method: Example D 0.2.1-0.3.0: pause stops feeding NDL v2 and keeps it loaded; 180 s 1080p H.264 + PCM over LAN HTTP
records.evidence: no black picture; the picture holds after the ~1 s queue plays out; resumed with beeps in sync with the flashes (owner, several pause/resume cycles)
records.limitations: the pause takes effect only after the queued lead (up to 1 s) has played

records.method: Example D 0.2.2-0.3.0: nothing flushed on seek; later PTS shifted to continue 200 ms after the last fed; controller clock starts after the backlog
records.evidence: no black picture, sound in sync after live and paused seeks and a burst of 5 quick seeks; the continuation point tracked real time (no backlog growth)
records.limitations: old content keeps playing for 0.5-0.8 s after the key press at a 1 s feeding lead

records.method: Example D 0.2.1: NDL_DirectVideoFlushRenderBuffer on seek, decoder kept loaded, PTS continued monotonically
records.evidence: returned 0 in 4-15 ms, no black picture, but no sound for the rest of the session although audio packets kept being accepted
records.limitations: not usable for seeking while it kills audio; whether a reload restores audio was not tested

records.method: Example D 0.3.1: Home while playing and while paused; NDL unloaded on Suspended, playback resumed on Resuming -> Running only if it was playing
records.evidence: NDL_DirectMediaUnload in 56-59 ms on Home; playing again 142 ms after the app returned (reload 122 ms), sound fine (owner); a viewer pause stayed paused and OK reloaded NDL in 83 ms
records.limitations: a paused session shows no picture after returning (the decoder was released)

records.method: Example D 0.4.0, bundled MKV with two SubRip tracks (English default, French two-line cues), drawn by SubtitleView over the NDL video plane
records.evidence: cues shown every 1.00 s in time with the flash and beep, switching English/French/off, seeks with subtitles on; readable size and outline (owner); frame interval 20 ms
records.limitations: text tracks only; bitmap subtitles (PGS/DVD/DVB), external files, ASS styling and non-Latin fonts untested on the TV

records.method: Example D 0.4.0-0.4.1, https://uploads.video-commander.com/sample/BigBuckBunny.mp4 (158 MB, 720p H.264 + AAC 44.1 kHz) and an AV1 clip from test-videos.co.uk, via the kit's HttpStream over the TV's libcurl
records.evidence: certificates verified with the system CA store; seekable (206), opened in ~0.5 s, feeding kept 0.5-1 s ahead with no reconnects; seeks worked
records.limitations: the 24 fps BBB judders on this TV (see media.ndl.frame_rate_24p); one internet server and one CDN only

records.method: Example D, 30 s 1080p25 test pattern with AAC 44.1 kHz decoded to PCM, NDL rate enum 2
records.evidence: smooth, beeps in sync with the flashes, same 1 kHz pitch (owner)

records.method: Example D 0.4.1, Big Buck Bunny 360p AV1 MP4 (video only, no audio track) over HTTPS
records.evidence: NDL_DirectMediaLoad(av1 640x360) -> 0, load/playing callbacks, played properly without an audio stream (owner)
records.limitations: 10 s 360p only; video-only playback was smooth here although earlier reports said NDL needs audio to pace

records.method: Example D: 24 fps BBB (internet and LAN), a 24 fps test pattern, the same BBB retimed to 25 fps; NDL video.unknown1 set to 24
records.evidence: 24 fps BBB judders on camera pans (internet and LAN alike, feeding never starved); retimed to 25 fps it is smooth; the 24 fps test pattern looked smooth (little motion); unknown1=24 was accepted and changed nothing
records.limitations: NDL v2 has no frame-rate field; PlxNative declares Starfish adaptiveStreaming.maxFrameRate and measured 13 fps presented for 24p declared at 60 vs 24.1 declared at 24. The TV's Real Cinema setting could not be found on this unit

records.method: Example D 0.4.2 (per-stream lanes, priming): Tears of Steel 720p H.264 + MP3 44.1 kHz (decoded to PCM) streamed over HTTPS from download.blender.org; Big Buck Bunny retimed to 25 fps over LAN
records.evidence: dialogue in lip sync, also after seeks; smooth at 25 fps; pause and seeks fine (owner)
records.limitations: 24 fps content still judders on pans (media.ndl.frame_rate_24p)

records.method: Example D 0.5.0 {"backend":"starfish"}: StarfishMediaAPIs from a dlopened libplayerAPIs.so.1 under Developer Mode, SDL-webOS exported window, BUFFERSTREAM Load; 24 fps Big Buck Bunny 720p H.264 + AAC (ADTS, passed through) over LAN HTTP
records.evidence: exported window _Window_Id_11 placed rv=1; Load -> 1 in 330 ms with VDEC and ADEC allocated; pipeline reported frameRate 24; first frame ~0.6 s after Load; displayed-frame counter (type 49) 5,5,5,5,4 per 200 ms = 24 fps; owner: pans smooth (no judder), sound in sync, real Pause/Play, seeks and Back fine; position from FRAMEREADY; 6+ minutes
records.limitations: H.264 + AAC only so far; HEVC, AC-3/E-AC-3, HTTPS, background/foreground and long sessions untested; objects are never freed (64 KiB per Load)

records.method: Example D 0.5.1 on Starfish: quick repeated Right/Left presses with a 400 ms settle window before feeding a splice seek's target
records.evidence: 0.5.0 played a piece of every intermediate seek point (owner); 0.5.1 jumps straight to the final point (owner)

records.method: Example D 0.6.1 AutoBackend(Starfish, NDL): the five bundled clips in one session, Back to the list between them, then Home and return
records.evidence: H.264 + AAC, HEVC + AC-3 5.1 (passed through) and the subtitle clip chose Starfish; H.264 + MP3 (MPEG-TS) fell back to NDL with MP3 decoded to PCM; all in sync, subtitles drawn over the Starfish video, Home and return resumed (owner)
records.limitations: the backend is chosen from codecs only; AV1/VP9 rely on NDL

records.method: Example D 0.6.0 vs 0.6.1: Starfish Loads in sequence (HEVC, H.264, HEVC) with and without the object destructor after UnloadCompleted
records.evidence: 0.6.0 (no destructor): the third Load got no decoder resources and blocked; 0.6.1 (destructor after type 23): every Load started
records.limitations: a playback thread that cannot be stopped within the deadline is detached and can outlive its controller (crash seen after the 0.6.0 hang)

records.method: Example D 0.6.1 (AutoBackend chose Starfish): Big Buck Bunny 596 s 720p24 H.264 + AAC over HTTPS from uploads.video-commander.com, played to the end without input
records.evidence: 14315 video and 25666 audio packets fed, no reconnects, warnings or Full retries; pushEOS then Ended at 598.9 s; displayed-frame counter mean 4.81 per 200 ms (24.0 fps); UI frame interval 16.66 ms
records.limitations: one stream, one session

records.method: Example D 0.7.0 AutoBackend: FfmpegSource decodes audio Starfish cannot take and re-encodes it with FFmpeg's native AC-3 encoder (libswresample for rate and layout); bundled clips H.264 + 7.1 FLAC 96 kHz (MKV) and H.264 + Opus stereo 48 kHz (MKV)
records.evidence: both chose Starfish (Load codec audio AC3, ADEC allocated); FLAC became AC-3 5.1 48 kHz 640 kb/s, Opus AC-3 stereo 256 kb/s; beep in sync with the flash on both (owner); encoder thread CPU 90 ms per s of audio (9.0% of a core) for 7.1 96 kHz, 15.3 ms (1.5%) for stereo 48 kHz
records.limitations: CPU excludes decoding; TrueHD, DTS and PCM tracks verified on the host only; ~5 ms AC-3 encoder delay not compensated

records.method: Example D 0.8.0 AdaptiveSource on Starfish: Dolby DV/Atmos test DASH (SegmentTemplate, 2160p59.94 HEVC + E-AC-3 JOC), Apple bipbop HEVC HLS (fMP4 byte ranges, separate AAC), Mux x36xhzz HLS (MPEG-TS, muxed AAC), Shaka angel-one DASH (SegmentBase/sidx, AAC); single and held Left/Right seeks, Back
records.evidence: Dolby: 3840x2160 HEVC with E-AC-3 passed through, first frame ~1.7 s after launch, position advancing 1 s/s with ~60 video frames fed per second over 40 s, no retries; picture and sound in sync on all four, seeks resume on all four (owner)
records.limitations: plain HEVC rendition only: the TV showed HDR, not Dolby Vision (DV not declared to Starfish yet); fixed bitrate (no switching); held-key seeks needed a fix (interrupted reopen) and Apple's misaligned audio/video segments needed audio trimmed to the video keyframe, both in this version

records.method: Example D 0.9.0: Dolby DV/Atmos test DASH (DV profile 8.1 HEVC 2160p59.94, E-AC-3 JOC) on Starfish with contents.DolbyHdrInfo {trackType single, encryptionType clear, profileId 8} and contents.immersive ATMOS, both gated on com.webos.service.config (supportDolbyHDRContents, supportDolbyTVATMOS = true)
records.evidence: dvvC read from the init segment (profile 8, compatibility 1); pipeline video info hdrType DolbyVision (was none without the node in 0.8.0), audio info immersive ATMOS; the TV showed Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos with picture and sound fine (owner)
records.limitations: profile 8.1 only; profile 5, PlxNative's 1 ns PTS nudge for DV LUT lookups (measured on webOS 4.10.2) and ACB's Atmos read-out are not examined on this TV

records.method: Example D 0.10.0 AdaptiveSource with bitrate switching on Starfish (adaptiveResolution declared): Mux x36xhzz HLS-TS (five rungs 288p-1080p, 10 s segments) from initial_bandwidth 6 Mb/s; Unified Streaming Tears of Steel HLS-TS over a slow link
records.evidence: Mux: started 1280x720 2.1 Mb/s, estimate 61.7 Mb/s after the first segment, switched to 1920x1080 6.2 Mb/s at segment 2 (20 s); pipeline reported 1920x1080 and playback continued 1 s/s; no visible glitch (owner). Tears of Steel: estimate 0.5 Mb/s, switched from 1680x750 2.5 Mb/s down to 224x100
records.limitations: video only (audio renditions do not switch); H.264 size changes only tried

records.method: Example D 0.10.1 vs 0.10.2 on Mux HLS-TS: held Right (about 150 coalesced seeks), single presses and Left; Starfish callbacks 48 (dropped frames per 200 ms poll on webOS 5+, PlxNative's decompile) logged in full
records.evidence: 0.10.1: after a held-key burst the sink reported 6-19 dropped frames per poll for as long as playback ran, with audio dropping out every few seconds (owner): new content was spliced behind the decoder's clock. 0.10.2 places it after the clock estimated from FRAMEREADY: the burst left at most a few drops, audio continuous (owner)
records.limitations: two single seeks about 2 s apart still produced roughly 8 s of dropped-frame reports before recovering on their own; not yet explained

records.method: Example D 0.11.0 AdaptiveSource subtitle loader: Apple bipbop HEVC HLS (WebVTT segments with X-TIMESTAMP-MAP MPEGTS:900000), Shaka angel-one DASH (wvtt in MP4 behind a sidx, four languages)
records.evidence: Apple: English track chosen as default, 600 cues from 75 files; cues in time with the picture's bip/bop and Down toggles them (owner); Shaka: dialogue subtitles shown and Down cycles languages (owner)
records.limitations: files are fetched one at a time in playback order (Apple: ~55 s for 600 s of cues), so a far seek soon after opening may show none for a while; TTML not readable; Greek and other non-Latin scripts depend on the bundled fonts

records.method: Example D 0.12.1 AdaptiveSource live on Starfish: DASH-IF livesim2 testpic_2s (dynamic MPD, SegmentTemplate @duration, 1 min time-shift, UTCTiming http-xsdate) and Unified Streaming live HLS (MPEG-TS, separate renditions)
records.evidence: livesim2: server clock +1035 ms from the TV's, joined at 54 s of a 60 s window, position advancing 1 s/s with displayed-frame callbacks once the first packet was mapped near 0 (0.12.0 held the first frame); smooth with sound, LIVE label, Left/Right seeks within the window; Unified HLS live also plays (owner)
records.limitations: startup about 4.5 s from launch to first frame on livesim2; live subtitles not loaded; Akamai's public HLS live test master pointed at a missing variant (404) on 2026-10-12

records.method: Example D 0.12.1 vs 0.12.2 (pooled curl connections, renditions opened in parallel): launch with autoplay, time from the player's play line to Starfish's first presented frame in the event log
records.evidence: livesim2 live DASH: 6.3 s -> 3.1 s; Dolby DASH VOD: 0.9 s; Unified Streaming live HLS: 6.9 s, bound by that server from this network (TCP connect 1.6 s, 0.8 Mb/s against a 1.3 Mb/s starting rung)
records.limitations: the first HLS open is still sequential (the audio lane needs the video's timeline origin); the starting rung comes from initial_bandwidth, not a measurement

records.method: Example D 0.13.0: DASH-IF livesim2 timesubswvtt_en/testpic_2s (dynamic MPD with a live wvtt AdaptationSet) on Starfish, subtitles switched on with Down, a Left seek within the window
records.evidence: a cue every second with the UTC time, in step with the clock burnt into the picture, still updating after the seek (owner)
records.limitations: HLS live WebVTT verified on the host only (no public live HLS with subtitles found)
